newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Russia, Israel said negotiating aircraft deal.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Israel said negotiating aircraft deal.

text.p: Russia will soon decide on the sale of an Ilyushin 76 aircraft to Israel that would be transformed into a spy plane and resold to China, the daily Haaretz reported on Tuesday.
The Israeli newspaper said the sale of the aircraft to China was part of a deal valued at $250 million but did not provide more details on the deal.
It said billionaire Shoul Eisenberg, chairman of the powerful Israel Corp conglomerate, was brokering the deal with China and recently updated Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI) about the sale.
Officials in Eisenberg's office declined to comment on the report. Eisenberg, who lived many years in China, has brokered numerous business deals with China.
Government-owned IAI plans to fit the heavy freighter with special electronic and radar systems to transform it into an early warning aircraft for intelligence use, Haaretz said.
A similar aircraft was recently sold to Chile, the paper said.

The sale of the Russian aircraft to Israel is essential to the deal with China because of its performance and price, the newspaper said. Other alternatives produced by Boeing Ba.N and Airbus have been turned down by the Chinese.
An IAI spokeswoman declined to comment on the report.

Haaretz quoted IAI chairman Avigdor Ben Gal as saying: "The issue is at a stage of final decision in Russia. The negotiations with Russia for the sale of the Ilyushin are secret and have a strategic significance for Chinese-Israeli relations. All publications could hurt the successful outcome of the deal."
China established diplomatic ties with Israel in February 1992, ending years of political estrangement linked to the Communist government's support of Palestinian statehood.

Persistent reports of secret arms sales date back many years. In the late 1980s Israel was rumoured to have helped Chinese defence industries produce an air-to-air missile, that Pentagon officials said they suspected was based on the U.S. Sidewinder.

In recent years Israel was rumoured to have given U.S. technology to China to build advanced fighter planes. Israel and China denied the rumours but the Jewish state has confirmed having "security relations" with Beijing.
Last year Defence Ministry Director General David Ivri said Israel had sold China "some technology on aircraft".
Last December IAI said that for the first time it was carrying out maintenance work on commercial aircraft belonging to China.
